provenance.note: Claim-dataset compilation: each record names its source, date and flag (verified / our analysis / as asserted); empty sources by design - per-record citations carry accountability.

attribution.osm: Centerline and width measurement derived from OpenStreetMap (ODbL).
attribution.sentinel: Chips and corridor metrics contain modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026).

claims.text: A new check dam across the Cooum at Perambakkam was sanctioned in February 2026: Rs 5.98 crore, 85 m long, 3.38 Mcft storage, 359.12 acres of ayacut, designed for a flood discharge of 10,556 cusecs at the site; the order places Kesavaram anicut 7.7 km upstream and the Puthumavilangai check dam 5 km downstream
claims.source: G.O.(Ms) No.15, WRD (S2), 13 Feb 2026

claims.text: The Cooum originates at the junction of the Old Bangaru Channel with the surplus courses of the Cooum and Satharai tanks; WRD gives the river 65 km from here to the sea.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, sections 1.1.3 and 1.2

claims.text: Fresh water enters the river only when Poondi reservoir reaches its full level: 650 cusecs are diverted through Kesavaram anicut for 75 to 90 days, about 51.68 MCM in such a year.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.7

claims.text: Kesavaram anicut itself stands across the Kosasthalaiyar, not the Cooum; its regulated arm runs about 5 to 7.5 km before it becomes the Cooum - the same DPR calls it the Placis Canal (5 km) in one section and the Old Bangaru Channel (7.5 km) in another. Its construction date is not stated in any primary on our record.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum and Kosasthalaiyar Sub Basin DPRs

claims.text: OpenStreetMap maps no water surface on the first seven kilometres; outside the diversion season the channel here runs dry.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu OSM and Sentinel-2 analysis

claims.text: The river takes its name from Koovam village in Tiruvallur district, which stands on this stretch with its Tripuranathar temple and temple tank.
claims.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8; Wikimedia Commons records

claims.text: WRD's rain gauges record 712.78 mm a year at Kesavaram anicut and 1,207.97 mm at Korattur anicut.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR

claims.text: Of the sub-basin's 9,937.55 ha of registered tank ayacut, 6,629.52 ha remained available at the DPR; the entire 3,308 ha loss lies in Tiruvallur district, the river's upper country. In Villivakkam block, eleven tanks with 1,376.26 ha of registered ayacut are recorded with present available ayacut nil.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, ayacut tables

claims.text: OpenStreetMap maps the river surface here 53 to 321 m wide at the per-km median, the widest mapped water on the river; 2.8 ha of open water shows from orbit this window, and 86% of the mapped surface reads as vegetation.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu OSM transects and Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: WRD records the Aranvoyal anicut downstream of this bed 'in fully dilapidated condition' due to illegal sand mining in the river, serviceable only by full reconstruction.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.1.5

claims.text: Aranvoyal anicut is recorded by WRD in fully dilapidated condition after illegal sand mining, serviceable only by full reconstruction
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.1.5

claims.text: Korattur anicut's New Bangaru Canal offtake to Chembarambakkam: 7.65 km, maximum 3,627 cusecs
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR

claims.text: Aranvoyal anicut (WRD chainage 45.33 km from the mouth) was built to feed Thiruninravur and Gudapakkam tanks; WRD records that the Cooum's two anicuts no longer serve any irrigation command in the sub-basin.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, sections 1.1.5 and 1.7

claims.text: Korattur anicut diverts Cooum water out to Chembarambakkam tank in the Adyar sub-basin through the 7.65 km New Bangaru Canal, maximum capacity 3,627 cusecs; CRRT states the transfer in the present tense.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR; CRRT Cooum River Restoration page

claims.text: Korattur anicut was reported under reconstruction in 2021: Rs 32 crore, NABARD-funded, begun January 2021 and 80% complete by that August, per press reports; no completion statement or government order is on the public record.
claims.source: Press reports, 2021 (no G.O. located)

claims.text: The Krishna water link canal from Poondi to Chembarambakkam crosses the Cooum at Aranvoyal anicut and gathers some of its water on the way.
claims.source: IISc/IIT-M/IIT-B, Chennai Floods 2015: A Rapid Assessment

claims.text: 39.6 ha of open water shows from orbit on this reach this window, the largest on the river; it carries one of the four suspended-sediment readings the river's open water allows.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: 15.3 ha of open water and a 52% vegetation share on the mapped water surface this window.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: The check dam pool is the ICRERP's upstream limit; the programme's stated scope runs 32 km from here to the mouth
claims.source: CRRT, Cooum River Restoration page

claims.text: The Paruthipattu check dam is the upstream limit of the Integrated Cooum River Eco-Restoration Project: 'from Paruthipattu check dam to the river mouth in the Bay of Bengal', a stated 32 km.
claims.source: CRRT, Cooum River Restoration page

claims.text: 94.8% of the mapped water surface at the check dam pool reads as vegetation from orbit this window, the highest share on the river.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: A PWD environmental-cell sampling point sits downstream of the bridge on the Poonamallee-Avadi road near Paruthipattu.
claims.source: WRD/PWD TN IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, section 1.7 sampling table

claims.text: WRD's frame for its seven ICRERP restoration works runs from Paruthipattu Anicut to the confluence point, about 27 km, with Rs 135.57 crore allotted to the department; six works (Reaches 2 to 7) at an estimated Rs 79.93 crore are recorded completed
claims.source: WRD Policy Notes 2024-25 and 2025-26

claims.text: PWD desilting and baby-canal formation, non-CRZ stretch (Ch. 9,677-27,336 m from the mouth): fully completed
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ), as on 30.06.2021

claims.text: Thiruverkadu Municipality removed 1,648 MT of solid waste along the riverside; Senneerkuppam, Adayalampattu and Vanagaram panchayats removed 4,582 cubic metres and fenced 1.92 km
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: Thirumazhisai Town Panchayat 3 MLD STP: consented discharge of treated sewage into the river downstream of the Paruthipattu check dam
claims.source: TNPCB OCMMS consent order 62519837

claims.text: PWD's desilting and baby-canal formation on the non-CRZ stretch (chainage 9,677 m to 27,336 m from the mouth) was reported fully complete by June 2021; the baby canal provides a minimum ecological flow path.
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ), progress as on 30.06.2021

claims.text: CPCB's Poonamallee station sits on this reach: 2024 BOD ranged 8-24 mg/L, the lowest of the river's seven stations; mean COD rises station by station downstream, from 93.3 mg/L here to 140.0 near Central Jail.
claims.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2024 (detailed edition)

claims.text: Thirumazhisai Town Panchayat's 3 MLD STP is consented to discharge treated sewage 'into the Cooum River near the Thiruverkadu Minor Canal at the downstream of the Paruthipattu Check Dam' (order renewed 1 July 2026, valid to March 2028).
claims.source: TNPCB OCMMS consent order 62519837

claims.text: Maduravoyal tank diversion channel (962 cusecs, Rs 17.52 crore, sanctioned 2009-10): recorded by CAG as not commenced as of January 2017, with an alternate straight-cut alignment proposed
claims.source: CAG of India, Report No. 4 of 2017, para 5.1.7

claims.text: Modular STP Maduravoyal, 0.6 MLD: civil works at 14%
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: NGT (Mar 2026): WRD and NHAI to ensure no dumping of debris beyond what the Chennai Port-Maduravoyal Elevated Road Project strictly requires
claims.source: NGT (SZ) order via Down To Earth court digest (case number unconfirmed)

claims.text: 86% of the mapped water surface on this reach reads as vegetation this window; 246 buildings stand within 50 m of the centerline.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 and Google Open Buildings analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: A Rs 17.52 crore diversion channel from Maduravoyal tank to the Cooum (962 cusecs of surplus flood water) was sanctioned in 2009-10; CAG recorded it as not commenced as of January 2017 after the original alignment was built over, with an alternate straight-cut alignment proposed.
claims.source: CAG of India, Report No. 4 of 2017, para 5.1.7

claims.text: In its judgment of 24 March 2026 the NGT directed that WRD's permission to NHAI for the Chennai Port-Maduravoyal Elevated Road Project along the river carry adequate precautionary and flood-mitigation measures, particularly during the monsoon, with GCC and CRRT continuing eco-restoration.
claims.source: NGT (SZ) judgment in O.A. 121 of 2024, 24 Mar 2026

claims.text: Consented treated-sewage discharges to the river: Koyambedu 34 MLD and 60 MLD STPs, the 120 MLD plant's balance and the 45 MLD TTRO chain via a PWD canal; trade effluent NIL on every order
Underground sewerage scheme, Nerkundram: works at 32%
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: The consented discharges into the Cooum are municipal: CMWSSB's 34 MLD and 60 MLD Koyambedu STPs discharge to 'River Coovum', and the 120 MLD plant's remaining treated sewage and the 45 MLD TTRO plant's chain reach the river through a PWD canal. Every one of those orders records trade effluent NIL.

Across 11,583 granted water consents from the five Cooum-corridor TNPCB district offices (2021-2026), fifteen orders name the Cooum as a point of disposal, covering seven facilities, all municipal sewage plants. Nine industrial units near the river hold orders that expressly prohibit discharge of sewage or trade effluent to the Cooum.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu review of the TNPCB OCMMS granted-consent register

claims.text: CMWSSB's underground sewerage scheme at Nerkundram, on this reach's north bank, stood at 32% in June 2021 and 96% in the state's February 2024 status report.
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ); CRRT status report to the NGT, 01.02.2024

claims.text: Interception and diversion packages V, VIII and X (Anna Nagar, Aminjikarai): 100% complete and commissioned; package IV (Metha Nagar) at 84%
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: Package IX (NSK Nagar): shelved due to encroachments existing along the alignment
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: The February 2024 status report records the NSK Nagar encroachment removed and the outfalls at the location plugged, with eleven of thirteen interception packages complete
claims.source: CRRT status report to the NGT in O.A. 299/2013 with connected matters (SZ), 01.02.2024

claims.text: TNSCB's December 2015 snapshot: 22.7 of 80 bank-km encroached, 16,820 encroachments, 14,257 families - the frame every later progress number counts against
claims.source: CAG of India, Report No. 4 of 2017, Chart 4.1 (TNSCB data)

claims.text: 722 buildings stand within 50 m of the centerline on this one reach - more than one in three of the river's total - and 2,963 within 100 m.
claims.source: Google Open Buildings v3 (confidence >= 0.7); Neer Vazhvu proximity analysis

claims.text: Three CPCB stations sit on this reach (Anna Nagar, Arumbakkam, Aminjikarai). The Aminjikarai station's 2021 maximum BOD was 345 mg/L; the 2024 maximum across all seven river stations is 54 mg/L.
claims.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2021 and 2024

claims.text: 17% of the mapped water surface here reads as vegetation this window, against 81 to 86% on the suburban run upstream.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: CRRT nature trail: 1.5 km elevated boardwalk, College Road bridge to Munroe bridge, work begun 2018
claims.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8

claims.text: Packages II (Chetpet) and III (Nungambakkam): 100% complete, with outfalls to be plugged after commissioning of the STP
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: Modular STPs under CRRT: Chetpet 1.0 MLD and Choolaimedu 1.2 MLD, consented to discharge treated sewage to the river (valid to March 2028)
claims.source: TNPCB OCMMS consent orders 44586514, 48668507

claims.text: PWD gives the river's tidal influencing range as mouth to Chetpet, about 9.4 km; the ICRERP's CRZ-stretch boundary (chainage 9,677 m) lands almost exactly here.
claims.source: CMDA Seminar on Waterways in Chennai (Mar 2010); GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016

claims.text: HSCTC's field survey found this belt holding roughly half its survey-era width: College Bridge to Mc. Nicholas Road measured 99-118 m in the survey records and 47-53 m on the ground in about 2012.
claims.source: HSCTC feasibility report (c. 2012), via the Wikipedia width table of 25 Aug 2013

claims.text: A 1.5 km elevated boardwalk between College Road bridge and Munroe bridge, modelled on the San Antonio River Walk, began work in 2018 under CRRT.
claims.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8

claims.text: Eight trash booms deployed across the city river, including near the Buckingham Canal and behind Madras Medical College
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: GCC river fencing: 13.75 of 23.92 km (Jun 2021), 18.4 km (Feb 2023)
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016; Citizen Matters (TNUHDB/CRRT figures)

claims.text: Langs Garden 10 MLD STP: civil works at 30.7% in June 2021; 97% in the February 2024 status report
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ); CRRT status report to the NGT, 01.02.2024

claims.text: Chintadripet 10 MLD modular STP under CRRT: consented to reuse (railway yard and avenue plantation), not the river
claims.source: TNPCB OCMMS consent orders 59517520, 64956326

claims.text: CPCB's Central Jail station records the river's lowest 2024 readings: dissolved oxygen 0.3 mg/L in every sample, BOD 15-54 mg/L, mean COD 140 mg/L. The 2024 edition publishes no coordinates for this station.
claims.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2024 (detailed edition)

claims.text: The 10 MLD Chintadripet modular STP under CRRT is consented to supply treated water to the railway yard and Corporation avenue plantation - reuse, not the river (orders of 2024 and 2025).
claims.source: TNPCB OCMMS consent orders 59517520, 64956326

claims.text: Eight trash booms were deployed across the city river by June 2021, including near the Buckingham Canal and behind Madras Medical College; the NGT's judgment of 24 March 2026 records the river's compound wall at 20.54 km completed of a total 23.92 km.
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016; NGT (SZ) judgment in O.A. 121 of 2024, 24 Mar 2026

claims.text: Mouth works: Rs 70.00 crore sanction for continuous opening and desilting, mouth to Napier Bridge (G.O.(Ms) No.76, MAWS (MC-I), 31 Jul 2020)
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ)

claims.text: NIOT-designed curved training walls, 265 m north and 310 m south, with 3,05,000 cubic metres of capital dredging, cleared September 2022
claims.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III

claims.text: Reach-1 mouth works (chainage 0-700 m, revised cost Rs 70 crore): 95% complete in WRD's Policy Note 2024-25; 'all Works have been Completed' in the 2025-26 note
claims.source: WRD Policy Notes 2024-25 and 2025-26

claims.text: Boundary demarcation of the Adyar, Cooum (Reach-I) and Buckingham Canal using differential GPS, taken up under CRRT fund at an estimated Rs 3.87 crore, is recorded completed
claims.source: WRD Policy Note 2025-26

claims.text: The clearance's own conditions: a three-year fisheries study and three years of salinity and marine-ecology monitoring at the mouth - no known public copy of either series
claims.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III, conditions

claims.text: The Buckingham Canal crosses the river here (canal chainage km 16.9-19.2, that page's reach 6); the two waterway pages link to each other at this junction.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu waterway geometry (OSM-derived centerlines)

claims.text: WRD's submission to the coastal-zone appraisal records that the river's bed levels near the mouth have fallen below mean sea level and that further desilting would not be useful against the continuously forming sand bar. The works cleared in September 2022 are a pair of curved, NIOT-designed training walls of 265 m and 310 m, with 3,05,000 cubic metres of capital dredging.
claims.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III, 15 Sep 2022

claims.text: The same clearance mandates a three-year fisheries study and three years of salinity and marine-ecology monitoring at the mouth; no known public copy of either series exists yet.
claims.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III, conditions

claims.text: WRD's Policy Notes record the Reach-1 mouth works (chainage 0-700 m, revised cost Rs 70 crore) at 95% in 2024-25 and 'all Works have been Completed' in 2025-26; the state's February 2024 status report records the curved training walls under the same package.
claims.source: WRD Policy Notes 2024-25 and 2025-26; CRRT status report to the NGT, 01.02.2024

claims.text: CPCB's Napier Bridge station records conductivity up to 15,820 umho/cm in 2024, against roughly 2,000 at the upstream stations, reflecting the tidal estuary.
claims.source: CPCB NWMP, Water Quality of Rivers 2024

claims.text: The Cooum runs 62.9 km from its origin near Satharai to the sea at Chennai, measured here end to end, fifty metres at a time. Its fresh water arrives by diversion, its city stretch is tidal, and the state files its water quality to the NGT every month.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: The Cooum rises at the junction of the Old Bangaru Channel with the surplus courses of the Cooum and Satharai tanks. Fresh water enters only when Poondi reservoir reaches its full level, at 650 cusecs for 75 to 90 days (WRD), and the upstream tanks' available irrigation command has fallen from 9,938 ha registered to 6,630 ha.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Between km 17.5 and 31 the river holds its only upstream open water, behind the Aranvoyal and Korattur anicuts and the Paruthipattu check dam. WRD records Aranvoyal as not serviceable after sand mining; Korattur diverts Cooum water to Chembarambakkam through the New Bangaru Canal; the check dam is the upstream limit of the Integrated Cooum River Eco-Restoration Project.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: From Paruthipattu to Koyambedu, 81 to 86% of the mapped water surface reads as vegetation in the Jun-Aug 2026 Sentinel-2 window. At Koyambedu the consented inflows begin: CMWSSB's treated sewage, with trade effluent recorded NIL on every order that names the river. No industrial consent names the Cooum as a point of disposal.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: The state files Cooum water quality monthly to the NGT: BOD 13-24 mg/L across seven locations in May 2026, against the bathing-water standard of 3 mg/L. The CPCB annual series runs to 2024; the TNPCB CCWW report's last published edition covers 2022-23.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: The HSCTC field survey (c. 2012) measured the city stretches at roughly a third to a half of their survey-era widths. The state's February 2024 status report records eleven of thirteen interception packages complete, the Langs Garden treatment plant at 97% and the Nerkundram sewerage scheme at 96%.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: TNSCB's December 2015 enumeration recorded encroachment on 22.7 of 80 bank-kilometres, with 14,257 project-affected families; 13,056 had been resettled by mid-2022 (Madras High Court record) and 13,484, with 773 remaining, by the state's February 2024 filing - a figure TNUHDB's policy notes repeat unchanged through 2025-26. In July 2025 the Madras High Court recorded that the government wants to restore the river and that the project remains struck on account of the remaining encroachments; in February 2026 the Supreme Court directed a joint Revenue-PWD inspection with notice and objections within four months, with status quo on demolition and construction meanwhile.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: PWD's record lists twelve schemes for keeping the mouth open between 1890 and 2000. The current works, cleared in September 2022, are NIOT-designed training walls with a mandated three-year fisheries and salinity study; WRD's Policy Notes record the Reach-1 mouth works 95% complete (2024-25) and completed (2025-26).
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: The current administrative sanction is Rs 735.08 crore, with Rs 604.75 crore disbursed (MAWS Policy Note 2025-26). The 2024-25 note stated completion by October 2024 except remaining resettlement; the 2025-26 note states all restoration works are expected to be completed soon. The 2026-27 revised budget announced global tenders and a new DPR for the Cooum and the Adyar. On CRRT's Adyar creek restoration, the department reports a faunal count of about 424 species against 141 before restoration.
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu synthesis of the sourced dossier

claims.text: Earliest recorded proposal to clean the river, as recorded by Madras Musings
claims.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8

claims.text: Cooum Improvement Scheme inaugurated by CM C.N. Annadurai
claims.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8; The Federal

claims.text: Pleasure boat service with seven jetties; the experiment ended when the sand pump developed snags
claims.source: Madras Musings Vol. XXXII No. 8

claims.text: Chennai City River Conservation Project: interceptors, pumping and four STPs across six waterways; CMWSSB records all works completed, TN Department of Environment records Rs 395.67 crore spent
claims.source: CMWSSB CCRCP page (via Internet Archive); TN Dept of Environment NRCP page

claims.text: Adyar Poonga Trust renamed Chennai Rivers Restoration Trust, with a remit over the Cooum, Adyar, Kosasthalaiyar and Buckingham Canal
claims.source: CAG of India, Report No. 4 of 2017, para 3.3.1

claims.text: GoTN directs CRRT to prepare the Cooum restoration DPR
claims.source: CAG of India, Report No. 4 of 2017, para 3.3.2

claims.text: Integrated Cooum River Eco-Restoration Plan submitted: 69 sub-projects prepared by LKS India for CRRT, approved by the CRRT Board on 16 July 2014
claims.source: G.O.(Ms) No.9, MAWS (MC.I), 13 Jan 2015

claims.text: Administrative sanction for the 60 short-term ICRERP sub-projects across seven agencies, Rs 181.85 crore of it for resettlement
claims.source: G.O.(Ms) No.9, MAWS (MC.I), 13 Jan 2015

claims.text: NGT orders compensation for pollution of the Cooum, Adyar and Buckingham Canal
claims.source: The News Minute; DT Next (Feb 2019); case number unconfirmed

claims.text: Sanction for continuous opening of the river mouth and desilting, mouth to Napier Bridge
claims.source: G.O.(Ms) No.76, MAWS (MC-I), 31 Jul 2020, cited in the GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016

claims.text: CRZ clearance for the Cooum mouth training walls, with a mandated three-year fisheries study and salinity watch
claims.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III

claims.text: MAWS Policy Note records the ICRERP sanction and disbursement, with all works expected complete by October 2024 except remaining resettlement
claims.source: TN MAWS Department Policy Note 2024-25, para 8.2.1

claims.text: MAWS Policy Note 2025-26 records Rs 604.75 crore disbursed against the Rs 735.08 crore sanction; all restoration works 'expected to be completed soon'
claims.source: TN MAWS Department Policy Note 2025-26, para 8.2.1

claims.text: Supreme Court (S. Rajeshwari v. State of Tamil Nadu, 11 Feb 2026) modifies the Cooum encroachment-removal directions: a joint Revenue-PWD inspection with notice and objections within four months, with status quo on demolition and further construction meanwhile
claims.source: Supreme Court order of 11 Feb 2026 in civil appeals from SLP(C) 6184/2024 and 7849/2024

claims.text: Revised Budget announces global tenders and a fresh DFR and DPR for rejuvenating the Cooum and the Adyar
claims.source: Revised Budget Estimates 2026-27, speech to the Legislative Assembly, 5 Aug 2026 (Dr. N. Marie Wilson, Minister for Finance, Planning and Development)

claims.text: 62.9 km - of river chained and measured from OpenStreetMap, origin to mouth; WRD's DPR gives the river 65 km from the same origin
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu OSM-derived centerline (Aug 2026 snapshot); WRD IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR

claims.text: 1,049 of 1,258 - transects return a measured water-surface width (every 50 m of chainage); the median is 70 m
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu transect measurement from OpenStreetMap water polygons

claims.text: 650 cusecs - diverted into the river through Kesavaram anicut for 75 to 90 days, when Poondi reservoir reaches its full level - the river's fresh-water inflow rule as WRD records it
claims.source: WRD IAMWARM Cooum Sub Basin DPR, sections 1.1.3 and 1.7

claims.text: 13-24 mg/L - BOD range across seven monitoring locations, May 2026, filed monthly to the NGT by the state; the bathing-water standard is 3 mg/L
claims.source: GoTN monthly progress report in NGT O.A. 673/2018 (TNPCB data), via NMCG

claims.text: Rs 604.75 crore - disbursed of the Rs 735.08 crore ICRERP sanction (Paruthipattu check dam to the mouth, 32 km)
claims.source: TN MAWS Department Policy Note 2025-26, para 8.2.1

claims.text: 15 orders - in the TNPCB consent register (2021-2026) name the Cooum as a point of disposal; all seven facilities are municipal sewage treatment plants. Nine industrial orders prohibit discharge to the river
claims.source: TNPCB OCMMS granted-consent register, five Cooum-corridor district offices, 2021-2026; Neer Vazhvu review of 11,583 orders

claims.text: WRD's submission to the coastal-zone appraisal: the river's bed levels near the mouth have already fallen below mean sea level, and further desilting there would not be useful because of the continuous formation of the sand bar.
claims.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III, recording WRD

claims.text: Sand deposition at the mouth, assessed at 1,75,000 cubic metres a year, is designed to fall to 8,000 cubic metres a year (4.57%) once the training walls are built; 3,05,000 cubic metres of capital dredging was cleared with them.
claims.source: MoEFCC CRZ clearance F.No.11-25/2022-IA.III

claims.text: The mouth works carry a Rs 70.00 crore administrative sanction for continuous opening and desilting from the mouth to Napier Bridge (G.O.(Ms) No.76, MAWS (MC-I), 31 July 2020), with the design tested on a physical model at IHH Poondi.
claims.source: GoTN status report in NGT O.A. 265 of 2016 (SZ), as on 30.06.2021

claims.text: The mouth works' recorded progression: curved training walls under progress in the state's status report of 1 February 2024; 95% complete in WRD's Policy Note 2024-25; 'all Works have been Completed' in the 2025-26 note.
claims.source: CRRT status report to the NGT (01.02.2024); WRD Policy Notes 2024-25 and 2025-26

claims.text: PWD's own record lists twelve schemes for sustained opening of the mouth between 1890 and 2000, from staged groynes to a 400 m tidal weir proposed at Napier Bridge in 1922.
claims.source: CMDA Seminar on Waterways in Chennai, Session III

claims.text: 333 ha - vegetation on the river corridor this window (weed mats, reeds and bank growth together)
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: ~63 ha - open water visible from orbit, concentrated at the Aranvoyal and Korattur anicut pools and the estuary
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 analysis, Jun-Aug 2026

claims.text: 4 of 13 - reaches hold enough open water for a suspended-sediment reading: the anicut pools and the estuary
claims.source: Neer Vazhvu Sentinel-2 NDTI analysis

claims.text: 1,903 - buildings within 50 m of the centerline (9,593 within 100 m); 722 of them on the reach between Anna Nagar and Aminjikarai (km 47.5-53.4). Counted from the centerline, not the river's recorded boundary
claims.source: Google Open Buildings v3 (2023 release, confidence >= 0.7); Neer Vazhvu proximity analysis
